title: Ingredientized cost tiles for session ledger export
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Design and prototype a compact, ingredientized tile system within the Redwood Console session ledger that breaks each session invocation into discrete cost ingredients (compute GPU token, KV cache hit/miss, prefix length multiplier, model variant uplift, quantization delta, network egress). These tiles will be exportable as a CSV and JSON mapping to accounting line items so finance and engineering teams can reconcile per-session spend with billing systems. Goal: improve traceability at token-level granularity while keeping the UI scannable for product and platform owners.
acceptance_criteria: Tiles show at least six cost ingredients with value, unit (tokens/ms/requests), and visual badge for high-impact (>15% of session cost)
CSV export maps each ingredient to a stable accounting SKU and includes normalization factors used (e.g., token weight, quantization multiplier)
Prototype tested in 3 usability sessions with PMs/finance and results documented with at least 3 actionable changes
Design includes failover state for when ingredient attribution is unavailable (graceful fallback to aggregated per-session cost)
Accessibility: tiles are keyboard focusable and read by screen readers with summarized aria-labels
comments: 2025-02-12 Aisha Patel: Kickoff - initial brief and goals. Put together two framing directions: 1) compact ingredient tiles (this ticket) for per-session view, 2) expanded lineage panel for per-route breakdown (separate ticket).
2025-02-13 Marco Chen: Reviewed edge cases - sessions that touch multiple model variants (fallbacks) need tile grouping. Also flagged engineering dependency on runtime attribution API (ENG-21021).

2025-02-14 Olivia Nguyen (PM): Suggested export should include both raw numbers and normalized 'cost units' for finance ingestion. Adding requirement to map to invoice SKUs. Marked customer_impact as medium.

2025-02-15 Design review: Shared low-fi mockups in Figma. Feedback from design lead (Jonas Mayer): ensure tiles remain legible at small widths and avoid more than three lines of text. Add micro-copy for 'why this ingredient matters'.

2025-02-16 Engineering sync: ENG asked for deterministic column names for CSV and an API contract example. I drafted a proposed CSV header mapping and dropped it in the attachments. ENG requested a sample payload from the runtime to validate export parsing.

2025-02-17 Usability plan: Schedule three 30-minute sessions with internal PMs and finance analyst. Test tasks: identify highest-cost ingredient, export CSV, and reconcile line to example invoice. Generate list of observed friction points.

2025-02-19 Usability findings (session 1/3): Users liked the ingredient labels but were confused by 'quantization delta' phrasing. Action: change to 'Model precision uplift' and add tooltip with simple explanation and example.
2025-02-19 Usability findings (session 2/3): Export file format OK, but finance asked for a stable 'line_item_id' field and a normalized 'cost_unit' column. Added to acceptance criteria.

2025-02-20 Design iteration: Updated hi-fi prototype with compact color-coded bars inside tiles showing relative contribution and an affordance to expand to route-level traces. Pushed updated frames to Figma (link in attachments).

2025-02-20 Marco Chen: Blocker note - ENG-21021 milestone slipped by two sprints; suggest shipping UI with a server-side aggregated fallback and wire export to aggregated CSV until attribution API is ready.

2025-02-20 Aisha Patel: Decision logged - proceed with incremental rollout: feature flag behind 'ingredient_tiles' with fallback and telemetry to track export usage. Create follow-up ticket to replace fallback when ENG-21021 is available.
